pr_records.title: Show and verify optional simultaneous CU8 + WAV recording in Satellite Center
pr_records.body:
Makes existing dual-format capability explicitly user-selectable and observable rather than merely showing two small checkboxes.

- In the main **Receiver & planner** select ISS SSTV 437.550 MHz. **Recording file formats · select one or both** now offers separate independent CU8 and WAV checkboxes, one-click **Select CU8 + WAV (both files)**, WAV-only, CU8-only shortcuts, and a live `aria-live` confirmation with number of output files. ISS still defaults to WAV; adding CU8 does not turn WAV off.
- After capture the on-screen result lists **both actual filenames** and whether each was saved to disk or a browser download was requested; two outputs are generated from the *same received WebUSB RF samples*, never synthetic data.
- In **Satellite Auto-Capture & Decode**, two dedicated checkboxes allow WAV and CU8 on the same ISS pass instead of the former fixed WAV-only choice; per-job size/format evidence and validation. Other mission types continue unchanged.
- In **Satellite Images & Data**, new independent WebUSB output checkboxes transfer the selection via same-tab sessionStorage into the main browser auto planner. No location or data embedded in URL. Native unattended ISS continues its already-implemented WAV path and is plainly labeled separately; this is not a claim that its one-receiver mode now simultaneously records two formats.
- Existing manually scheduled passes and calendar edits retain two independent formats; large dual recordings still use an explicit local folder picker and bounded streams.
- Added node tests verifying both options, dual pipeline, binary RIFF header, storage limits, automatic pass choices and cross-page transfer; cross-platform/ WebUSB CI enforces them.
- GitHub Pages will be synchronized only after CI verifies behavior; existing pages files not changed by this feature remain intact. No RF hardware/live ISS verification claimed.

pr_records.title: Satellite WebUSB: record actual FM-demodulated WAV and optional CU8 simultaneously
pr_records.body:

- ISS 437.550 MHz preset defaults to **FM WAV** instead of IQ; independent checkboxes for original CU8 and WAV, permitting WAV only, CU8 only or both. WAV is **real FM-demodulated audio during RTL-SDR WebUSB reception**, not renaming CU8 bytes; 48 kHz mono signed 16-bit PCM.
- Streamed DSP handles actual USB IQ blocks, retains quadrature/phase state across boundaries, writes correct RIFF header after real sample count is known; no uploaded/synthetic audio.
- Short WAVs remain bounded and downloadable. Long recordings use an explicit **local File System Access** picker (16 MiB memory cap). Simultaneously large WAV+CU8 uses a **single directory picker** to pre-authorize 2 disk streams without unsafe browser memory usage.
- Manual receiver, scheduled pass, scheduled edit and 60s ISS-only automatic browser jobs supported. Automatic ISS jobs now record WAV by default.
- Last WAV can be decoded in the existing Robot36 preview without re-importing; file imports and native companion continue to work. Long WAV files can be reopened manually for analysis.
- Tests verify actual simulated FM modulation to 1200 Hz PCM output, WAV header correctness, odd USB packet boundary continuity, safe 900s budgets, UI and scheduler integration. CI/Pages parity updated.

pr_records.title: Satellite processing: adaptive CPU/GPU/NPU selector with real WebGPU/CUDA Robot36 acceleration
pr_records.body:
Continues ISS Series 35 SSTV [PR #26](https://github.com/Tihulu/TIHULU-TEXT-CENTER/pull/26); keeps `main`, legacy reception, maps, calendar, archive and unrelated SDR apps untouched.

### Real implementation
- Adds **Auto · optimized for this device** (default) and **Custom CPU/GPU/NPU multi-select** to shared Signal Intelligence and Satellite Images & Data pages.
- Performs actual **WebGPU compute shader dispatch** for 1ms Robot36 PCM tone tracing (after a real IQ→FM audio step); CPU handles SSTV synchronization, pixels, preview, ZIP. Honest CPU fallback and stage reporting.
- Native companion probes **real CUDA/CuPy device compute**, uses optional NumPy CPU vectorization; persists compute mode/targets per scheduled pass and reports execution provenance. CPU+GPU hybrid permitted.
- **NPU is intentionally disabled** until a validated Robot36 DSP NPU kernel/model exists; an AI HAT/NPU appearing in inventory does not make generic non-ML SSTV decoding runnable there. No invented utilization.
- Adds tests for selector, CPU equivalence, native scheduler choices, UI and NPU rejection. Cross-platform CI wired.
- Docs: [compute acceptance details](https://github.com/Tihulu/TIHULU-TEXT-CENTER/blob/feature/satellite-compute-backends-2026-11-06/docs/SATELLITE_COMPUTE_BACKENDS.md).

### RF diagnosis
Current ARISS Series 35 **9–16 November 2026** is **437.550 MHz FM, Robot36**, not 145.800 MHz (that VHF frequency is historic/voice for other activities). A CU8 file does not contain its own center frequency/rate. 122,552,320 bytes implies 59.84 s at 1.024 MS/s or 29.92 s at 2.048 MS/s; no validated line sync is expected before the 9 Nov event. No claim of ISS RF reception.

### Still draft
Physical GPU throughput / Windows + macOS drivers / original WAV image correctness / GitHub Pages parity / live SDR acceptance not yet proven. Do not merge or advertise live release before these gates.

### Follow-up: event integrity and CU8 error diagnostics
- The official 9–16 Nov 2026 date envelope gates ISS Series 35 auto scheduling; exact activation times remain TBD, so a predicted pass alone is still not claimed active. Other ISS modes and manual operation remain available.
- Direct CU8 discovery distinguishes an old 145.800 MHz tuning from this campaign's announced 437.550 MHz, flags <36 s recordings, and notes if **file modification time** precedes Nov 9 (not proof of recording time). Previously observed 1200 Hz sync failure remains an honest absence of validation.
- New regression tests cover the date boundary and pre-event error context. Four portable OS test jobs previously passed after fixing NumPy-unavailable CPU selection; new event changes are under CI. `pages-source-parity` remains expected to fail until explicitly reviewed static changes are deployed to gh-pages.

pr_records.title: Satellite Center: automatic CU8 signal discovery (RF → analog audio → verified SSTV candidates)
pr_records.body:
## Continues Satellite Center PR #9 without losing existing image center
This draft integrates the existing Signal Intelligence enhancements from PR #17 into the **latest** Satellite Center source branch, preserving the new in-browser CU8→FM→Robot36 decoder, NASA imagery, WebUSB pass planner, orbit/map overlays and current companion.

### New automatic, fully local analysis
- User selects actual CU8 or the last real WebUSB capture and clicks **Automatic discovery · sound / image / data**.
- Reads every complete FFT window in bounded chunks, builds spectral/waterfall report, prioritizes the tuned center and strongest unknown energy bands.
- Tries narrow FM and AM, creates individually playable WAV candidates with frequency labels; never asserts that noise is human speech/music.
- For ≥33 s recordings at 1.024/2.048 MS/s, channelizes at candidate offsets and attempts real Robot36 1200 Hz line-sync validation, showing image candidates only after decoder sync checks (never fabricated pictures).
- Reports unsupported/unverified APRS and Meteor LRPT honestly; no CRC-verified packets claimed; exports local JSON evidence without raw audio/pixels; saves candidate audio and image on explicit user action.
- Shows progress, Cancel/Stop, file coverage, unknown frequency warnings, input limits. No uploads or background SDR scans.
- Existing manual CU8 analysis, spectrum selection, audio previews, source-only RF, GPS/TLE tracking, downloads and Image Center preserved.
- New synthetic tests and cross-platform CI across Linux/ARM, Windows, macOS.

### Boundaries
This is **not** universal modulation/protocol identification, guaranteed image reconstruction or receiver/source geolocation. A short recording such as 14.85 s cannot contain a complete 36 s Robot36 image. `CU8` has no embedded center frequency/sample rate. Browser file analysis is cross-platform; physical WebUSB still has browser/OS limitations.
See `satellite_center/SIGNAL_INTELLIGENCE.md`.

### Branch reconciliation / safety updates — 2026-11-06
- **Reconciled with PR #9** in two-parent merge commit `522429fa5bfa6a2a32dd55a1b7f91b50438eabbf`. This PR now descends from both feature heads and is mergeable against #9, without modifying `main` or removing the original Satellite Images & Data, calendar, TLE, or protocol features.
- Corrected scheduling so both operator-edited and automatic 60-second WebUSB captures **fit the predicted pass end** (`026ff64114143f4b36d5d11e259ccb8d351379c8`). A second runtime guard prevents late-awakened/contended browser sessions from starting a recording that cannot finish within LOS (`b5ea3e9fd420a77adf5fd7cc0e22bc76ca84dcd0`).
- Mirrored only affected browser assets to `gh-pages` (latest commit `2222a0a30bdd5d6c31a3eca37f5dad2893ee880f`). The 22 critical source/Pages browser assets were compared by Git blob SHA and **all matched** after the sync. This is source parity, not independent proof of a successful live site deployment.
- On earlier portable run `42288647028`, Linux x64, Linux ARM, Windows x64 and macOS jobs **passed**, but the Pages parity job failed during the before-sync window. Final portable CI rerun `42288854507` is **PASS (5/5 jobs)**: Ubuntu Linux x64, Ubuntu Linux ARM64, Windows x64, macOS 15 and `pages-source-parity`. Browser-only WebUSB and Text Center tests also passed at the current source head.

**Still DRAFT / NOT RELEASE-ACCEPTED:** Verify the final portable workflow including Pages parity, public URL and PWA cache, actual NESDR hardware + real satellite RF capture/decoding, device conflicts, per-OS drivers and native companion. These are not inferred from software CI.

PR #17 is an earlier fork superseded by this integrated proposal.

### Pass-aware capture length and media selection — November 6, 2026
- **New native capture budget:** `satellite_center/capture_budget.py` predicts full visible-window recording needs from actual AOS/LOS, 10 s lead, 4 s LOS margin, receiver protocol and free disk. Raw Meteor CU8 may run **up to 900 s / 2 GB** on the optional native companion, streamed to disk (1.024 MS/s ≈ 2.048 MB/s); manual capture remains limited to 240 s. A "full-pass-attempt" is not a full satellite dataset or successful RF demodulation.
- **Media-aware selection:** native Meteor LRPT → genuine raw IQ for optional SatDump; ISS SSTV → actual 48-kHz FM WAV for Robot36 attempt; ISS voice → actual 48-kHz FM WAV playback/export; APRS → installed rtl_fm + multimon-ng packet text (CRC and source not independently reverified). Default "prefer full visible pass" vs explicit quick 60 s sample is shown in both main/planner and Satellite Images & Data pages.
- **Feasibility/fallback:** estimated seconds, storage size, image/text/audio category and partial/full coverage appear on native armed job cards. When multiple requested formats are selected, prioritize feasible full-window content. If an optional decoder is missing, skip only the unavailable selected target. No automatic substitution outside the user's selected content.
- **Browser/PWA manual duration:** the pass planner's *Actual RF sample length* is now editable **1–900 s**. Small I/Q captures remain limited to **128 MiB RAM**; larger I/Q captures require **explicit, operator-selected local disk streaming** on supported secure Chromium/File System Access browsers, up to **2 GB** at the selected sample rate. At 2.048 MS/s that cap is 488 s, not 900 s. File permission is obtained during the scheduling gesture; tab must remain open, visible and awake. **Browser automatic WebUSB tasks remain 8–60 s** and must not claim a complete Meteor LRPT scene. Native unattended jobs can use the existing 8–900 s scheduling path. Unsupported browsers must use the native receiver for long captures.
- **Archive extraction:** preserve generic user WAV Robot36 attempts; native voice WAV has original playback and download without an assertion that speech or a spacecraft signal was detected.
- **Calendar + result archive:** cancelled jobs are hidden from the calendar while native audit records remain intact; hour rows now show local start/end, capture duration, longer interval bars and estimated output bytes. Pending jobs can change capture seconds. Both the main CU8 analysis and Satellite Images & Data views now allow inspection and ZIP export of actual decoded PNG/WAV, text, analysis JSON and evidence manifest (max 256 MiB outputs ZIP; raw huge IQ separate). Original source identity is not invented.
- **CI:** current source HEAD `9b2ba4e9629754da0a64c7c7e69e7d82d1b51c58` — [portable run 42299750105](https://github.com/Tihulu/TIHULU-TEXT-CENTER/actions/runs/42299750105) **PASS 5/5** after source-parity job rerun: Ubuntu x64, Ubuntu ARM64, Windows x64, macOS 15, and Pages/source parity. New source and `gh-pages` have **24 identical** critical browser assets (Pages commit `cbd192811be17b2663f976729aa19b440070264b`). Text Center and browser-only WebUSB CI also passed.
- **Still draft / hardware unverified:** live public Pages navigation/PWA cache not independently accessible from this environment; no physical NESDR SMArt v5, continuous 900 s capture, Meteor SatDump reception, ISS SSTV/APRS or cross-OS USB hardware acceptance completed. Retired NOAA APT stays archive-only. `main` unchanged.


### 2026-11-06 — Debian / Firefox native long-IQ fallback and calendar layout correction

- **Calendar overlap resolved:** the flex-column hourly timeline used to shrink each hour row to a small fixed height while tall job cards overflowed the following hours. Shared `browser.css` now disables flex shrinking on calendar hour rows, makes card height content-driven, and preserves job spans, clock ranges and cancel/edit controls. Node CSS regression checks included; latest stylesheet cache-busted for all browser/PWA clients.
- **704 MiB Firefox error:** existing browser-only WebUSB File System Access route is not supported in Firefox; the **Debian/Pop!_OS native SDR application** now acquires RTL-SDR with installed `rtl_sdr`, writes raw CU8 straight to disk, and serves the existing same-origin UI on `http://127.0.0.1:8791/`. No Chromium/JavaScript USB/file API or 128 MiB browser memory cap is involved. Native direct/manual and pass-scheduled IQ captures support **8–900 seconds / 2 GB maximum** (native rate 1.024 MS/s), subject to actual disk capacity, AOS/LOS margin and single receiver lock; unsupported modes/frequencies rejected. Browser pass cards can explicitly route to the native server using actual pass geometry. Browser-only Pages still needs Chromium for direct WebUSB; it displays an explicit native app alternative, not a fake 704 MiB memory buffer.
- **Standalone Debian USB bug fixed:** falling back on Text Center `textcenter.receivers` import previously made tuner detection always false and simulated a busy receiver when the main app was not installed. Native Debian now reads USB sysfs (0bda:2838) and scans active Linux receiver process executable names; no root, USB reset, signal fabrication or third-party process stopping.
- **Installable Debian artifact:** new `satellite_center/packaging/debian/build.sh` packages native Python dashboard, all shared browser assets, application launcher, icons, and distro dependencies `python3-skyfield` + `rtl-sdr`. **[Native Debian package run 42304639365](https://github.com/Tihulu/TIHULU-TEXT-CENTER/actions/runs/42304639365): SUCCESS**, built artifact **`tihulu-satellite-center-debian-native`** containing `tihulu-satellite-center_0.2.4~preview1_all.deb`. Debian 12 Docker **dpkg install + doctor + real HTTP GET** of native root, pass planner and reception workspace passed. User-local `install.sh` also defaults to this branch and makes native launcher primary; web-only Chromium launcher remains separate.
- **CI at HEAD `509d19d0249aa2eb1392d0b929be4fd49b1fbfae`:** [Portable run 42304633187](https://github.com/Tihulu/TIHULU-TEXT-CENTER/actions/runs/42304633187) **PASS 5/5** (Ubuntu x64, Ubuntu ARM64, Windows, macOS, Pages source parity). Additional [browser WebUSB](https://github.com/Tihulu/TIHULU-TEXT-CENTER/actions/runs/42304639043) and Text Center checks passed. Shared 24-browser-source-file `gh-pages` mirror committed `4f79d2d2996f5fb3ad397f1b63022fc0fcb26cea` without unrelated changes.
- **Acceptance still pending:** physical Nooelec NESDR SMArt v5 RTL-SDR continuous ~900 s test on user's Debian/Pop!_OS, Linux udev permissions/USB availability, sustained IQ disk throughput and actual Meteor/ISS decoder output. Synthetic CI and HTTP smoke alone are not hardware success. Remain **Draft**, do not merge into `main`.

## 2026-11-06 native desktop migration — Qt Widgets (0.3.0 preview1)

**Changed contract:** The installed Debian/Ubuntu/Pop!_OS application is a **real PyQt5/Qt Widgets GUI**, not a browser, localhost web page, Electron or WebView. Default `tihulu-satellite-center` and freedesktop launcher invoke `desktop`. Explicit `serve` retains the old optional localhost HTTP compatibility workflow only. Web/PWA remains separately available in its original project routes; do not delete or merge it into desktop.

**Implementation:** `satellite_center/desktop.py` provides six native tabs (Overview/USB; TLE/Passes with native date/frequency/duration; Auto reception; persisted calendar; real 8–900s rtl_sdr/rtl_fm/rtl_power capture; recordings/results with actual CU8 FFT/waterfall, image/audio/text previews, Meteor SatDump and provenance ZIP). Qt worker threads keep RF/network/FFT off the GUI thread. `native_analysis.py` processes genuine CU8 in bounded chunks, fast sampled overview or full-file spectral average, max 2GB; never identifies a satellite from FFT energy. `export_results_zip` includes only real PNG/JPG/WAV/TXT/JSON with manifest, not raw huge IQ.

**Packaging:** `satellite_center/packaging/debian/build.sh` now creates `tihulu-satellite-center_0.3.0~preview1_all.deb`; system Python3, PyQt5, NumPy, Skyfield, rtl-sdr required, qtwayland5 recommended for COSMIC Wayland. CLI `doctor` and explicitly selected `serve` preserved. User-local Linux installer now launches native Qt window and keeps browser shortcut separately. Desktop icon and Qt app identity added.

**Acceptance evidence:** Debian 12 Docker `.deb` install + headless Qt Widgets window smoke **PASS** on [native CI 42308833631](https://github.com/Tihulu/TIHULU-TEXT-CENTER/actions/runs/42308833631) and [42309006102](https://github.com/Tihulu/TIHULU-TEXT-CENTER/actions/runs/42309006102). Python 3.11/3.12/3.13 Text Center regression suite **PASS** after adjusting auto-mission synthetic tests on current series [42309459022](https://github.com/Tihulu/TIHULU-TEXT-CENTER/actions/runs/42309459022). Browser-only WebUSB tests also passed; Pages source unchanged by native migration.

**Still requires real hardware QA**: COSMIC Wayland visual/menu interaction, Nooelec RTL-SDR device/permissions, sustained 900s IQ disk capture, true ISS/Meteor decoding, and Windows/macOS native installer builds. Keep PR **Draft**, do **not** merge into `main` until accepted.

### 2026-11-07 — Qt desktop web feature-parity expansion (0.3.0~preview5)

This PR remains **Draft**. The installed Linux app uses **native PyQt5 Widgets (NO WebView, browser, Chromium/Electron or implicit localhost server)**. The separate Pages/PWA assets are preserved.

- **Real native maps:** Maps & Live includes bundled Natural Earth offline Earth chart, QPainter sky radar, optional operator-enabled OpenStreetMap HTTPS raster tiles for the visible viewport, mouse drag and cursor-anchored zoom, satellite pins and click-to-select, NORAD/name search, IMAGE/AUDIO/TEXT/RF candidate filters, follow, station center and fit-visible geometry, up to 12 live TLE ±45-min all-selected tracks, coverage overlays, 1-second live updates and pause/-45 to +90 minute time scrubber. Selected pin links to future native pass schedule. Visible map PNG and TLE-only GeoJSON export show explicit **orbital prediction, not measured RF**. No tile bulk download or fake satellite signal.
- **3-step reception workflow:** native Overview Auto Schedule & Capture → Analyze Recordings → Extract/Inspect/Save Results. Actual `.cu8` full/overview chunked FFT, waterfall, RF candidate discovery, FM IQ→WAV, WAV playback with optional Qt multimedia plugin, Robot36 SSTV PNG only with real sync, external SatDump Meteor, genuine image/audio/text previews, spectrum CSV/PNG and bounded evidence ZIP.
- **Locations and protocols:** the same 8,084 DE/TR offline cities + custom station coordinates, ISS event-only/Meteor LRPT media candidate chips and decoder requirements, native user-supplied 32-entry NORAD/protocol JSON catalog compatible with web import/export. User-provided frequencies are **unverified hints only** and never auto-run arbitrary receiver or decoder.
- **Auto compute parity:** native auto missions and Robot36 analysis expose Auto, CPU, CPU+GPU, CPU+NPU, CPU+GPU+NPU **requests** with capability-aware selection, not unverified accelerator claims. Native receiver remains actual `rtl_sdr`/`rtl_fm` hardware on disk with a single SDR lock.
- **User launchers:** installed Qt **System** launcher is default; old user Local/PWA shortcuts can be previewed via `tihulu-satellite-center cleanup-shortcuts`, and separately moved to reversible backups with `--apply`. Browser shortcut no longer created by default.

See [native/web capability & acceptance matrix](https://github.com/Tihulu/TIHULU-TEXT-CENTER/blob/feature/satellite-auto-discovery-integrated-2026-11-06/satellite_center/NATIVE_WEB_PARITY.md).

**Software QA:** most recent prior 0.3.0 preview4 native Debian package built and passed Debian 12 Qt offscreen smoke at [run 42318571029](https://github.com/Tihulu/TIHULU-TEXT-CENTER/actions/runs/42318571029). Latest preview5 CI is running/queued: [native Debian package 42318812551](https://github.com/Tihulu/TIHULU-TEXT-CENTER/actions/runs/42318812551), [portable matrix 42318812563](https://github.com/Tihulu/TIHULU-TEXT-CENTER/actions/runs/42318812563). Do **not** claim preview5 pass until these jobs finish successfully. Browser WebUSB & Text Center tests passed on preceding source. Physical Pop!_OS COSMIC + Nooelec RTL-SDR, sustained 900-second IQ, actual ISS/Meteor downlink/decoder success and native Win/macOS install packages remain unverified/not shipped. Do not merge `main`.


### 2026-11-07 — Native Qt recording/result format clarity · 0.3.0~preview6

- **No more ambiguous output listings:** Both local recordings and generated-results tables show explicit RAW RF · CU8, IMAGE · PNG/JPEG, AUDIO · WAV, TEXT · TXT, DATA · JSON, TABLE · CSV, MAP DATA · GeoJSON or ARCHIVE · ZIP labels instead of filename/extension alone.
- For PNG/JPEG/WAV, the Qt display checks actual local magic bytes and marks unreadable or unexpected headers; the file tooltip and details panel state that a recognizable file format is **not** independent proof of a complete decode, spacecraft transmitter or valid downlink.
- Added `satellite_center/native_data_labels.py` and cross-platform `tests/test_satellite_native_data_labels.py`; native offscreen Qt smoke now checks the format columns. User files are never uploaded or modified by these checks.
- Debian source package revision is **0.3.0~preview6**, with revised primary Qt launch/install instructions; historical localhost `serve` guidance explicitly marked opt-in and legacy.
- **CI links for latest head:** [Debian native package](https://github.com/Tihulu/TIHULU-TEXT-CENTER/actions/runs/42319556353), [cross-platform portable](https://github.com/Tihulu/TIHULU-TEXT-CENTER/actions/runs/42319556370), [WebUSB](https://github.com/Tihulu/TIHULU-TEXT-CENTER/actions/runs/42319556393), [Text Center](https://github.com/Tihulu/TIHULU-TEXT-CENTER/actions/runs/42319556524). Workflow results must be read live; do not infer a package PASS from a queued run.
- **Still Draft:** physical Pop!_OS/Nooelec receiver ownership and sustained capture, live ISS/Meteor RF/decoder validation, native Windows/macOS packaging and final GUI visual acceptance remain outside synthetic CI. Do not merge into `main`.


### 2026-11-07 — Web/PWA preview6 public Pages release VERIFIED

**Public URLs (browser edition, not embedded desktop Qt):**
- [Receiver, pass planner, Earth/Sky, signal analysis](https://tihulu.github.io/TIHULU-TEXT-CENTER/satellite_center/browser/)
- [Satellite Images & Data / local media](https://tihulu.github.io/TIHULU-TEXT-CENTER/satellite_center/browser/reception.html)

**Production evidence:**
- Reviewed source commit `d554d6790d08de1c3d7b399d6edbaa50f2226165` (PR #18 head).
- Published only the six modified static Satellite Center assets to `gh-pages` with single fast-forward commit `961abe2ef2c1b7041be8a0e305faf5fe518db6dc`; all existing other Pages applications preserved.
- [GitHub Pages build & deploy](https://github.com/Tihulu/TIHULU-TEXT-CENTER/actions/runs/42320162323): **SUCCESS**.
- [Independent public HTTPS smoke](https://github.com/Tihulu/TIHULU-TEXT-CENTER/actions/runs/42320347130): **SUCCESS** (fetches live HTML, CSS, JS and required preview6 markers).
- [Latest browser WebUSB tests](https://github.com/Tihulu/TIHULU-TEXT-CENTER/actions/runs/42320350462): **SUCCESS**.
- [Portable multi-OS + source/Pages parity](https://github.com/Tihulu/TIHULU-TEXT-CENTER/actions/runs/42320350511): **SUCCESS (5/5)** (Linux x64/ARM64, Windows, macOS, Pages/source parity).
- [Native Debian packaging](https://github.com/Tihulu/TIHULU-TEXT-CENTER/actions/runs/42320350452): **SUCCESS**, includes `tihulu-satellite-center_0.3.0~preview6_all.deb` in `tihulu-satellite-center-debian-native` Actions artifact.

**Web completeness of this pass:**
- Distinguishes actual Web/PWA experience from independent native PyQt5 desktop application and separate optional `serve` mode.
- New `file_format_inspector.mjs`: bounded local header checks for PNG/JPEG/GIF/WEBP/WAV/MP3/OGG/FLAC/MP4/WEBM, explicit CU8 IQ/raw, TXT/JSON/CSV. Malformed headers do not receive a fabricated decoded-media preview. No uploads and no receiver access.
- Format labels, provenance/tooltips, file evidence JSON, responsive CSS, new Node regression tests, static acceptance, and public Pages production smoke retained for future deployments.
- Existing WebUSB CU8+WAV dual recording, user-selected disk streaming, TLE-only maps/OSM overlay, editable calendar, Robot36 candidate results, official NASA imagery and media/protocol filters preserved.

**Still NOT validated in hardware:** browser WebUSB SDR, true ISS SSTV/NOAA/Meteor radio signal and long-duration capture, actual SatDump/AX.25 decoding, Pop!_OS/COSMIC Wayland GUI and physical Nooelec 900 s disk throughput. These require operator-owned hardware and real-world passes; synthetic CI is not evidence. Keep PR **DRAFT**, do not merge `main`.


### 2026-11-07 — Desktop Qt preview7 usability overhaul

The previous preview6 native Qt UI was significantly more confusing than the browser edition because it exposed eight engineering tabs and put RF analysis, decoded files, advanced settings and manual capture on one screen. **Preview7 restructures native Qt Widgets; no browser/Electron/WebView is introduced and no features are deleted.**

- **Five visible primary sections:** Home, Find satellites, Maps & live, Auto receive, Recordings & results. Reversible **More tools** menu retains Reception calendar, Manual RF capture and Saved protocols.
- **Guided native Home:** choose pass → schedule actual capture → open/inspect file → save real results, with direct shortcuts and visible passive SDR status.
- **One-click pass workflow:** image/audio/text/raw RF candidate badges and protocol explanations stay; the recording-detail form now opens only after selecting a candidate and pressing **Plan recording for this pass**. Scheduling success appears in the same screen.
- **Simplified Auto receive:** media checkboxes and a single explicit scheduling action are visible; max jobs, receive duration, elevation and CPU/GPU/NPU policy live in an expandable Advanced section. Success/skipped/blocked summaries display in place.
- **Results wizard:** Choose recording → Analyze RF → Decode & save, with persistent selected file banner, actual-file gate and accessible original NumPy FFT, discovery, FM WAV, Robot36 PNG, external SatDump, CSV/PNG/ZIP exports.
- **Maps & live:** default native Earth view with easy visible OpenStreetMap opt-in and station/fit actions; follow, elevation, coverage and track-scope options are available under Advanced map overlays; Sky radar remains available.
- **Direct receiver diagnostics:** actual USB report is shown from the Home screen instead of silently writing to another tab.
- **Visual acceptance:** Debian 12 offscreen Qt smoke and GitHub Actions now create five *real Qt UI* screenshots (synthetic TLE only) in independent artifact `tihulu-satellite-center-native-ui-preview7`. Package revision `0.3.0~preview7_all.deb`. Real COSMIC Wayland/Nooelec user acceptance remains pending.

**Do not merge `main` or claim real RF success.** Browser preview6 remains independently published and verified on `gh-pages`; these changes target the installed native app.


### Native preview7 screenshot inspection follow-up

Offscreen Debian CI successfully produced five genuine Qt screenshots, downloaded and inspected. Visual review identified and corrected three usability regressions after the initial preview7 build:
- Qt mnemonic parsing displayed ampersands as underscores in buttons/navigation (e.g. Maps & live, Decode & save, Auto schedule & capture). QPushButton, guided home groups and the step tab now escape `&` correctly.
- Oversized empty pass and archive tables consumed the screen, hiding the selected-pass details and next-step buttons. These lists now have bounded height and internal scrolling.
- Fitting a single orbital point could zoom the map to street level over open water, appearing empty. Auto-fit now caps at a regional Earth view (manual zoom retains detail and optional OSM streets).

Improved Qt card-label transparency and slightly larger base typography. Rebuilt headless screenshots and final native package are part of the most recent preview7 GitHub Actions runs; do not claim final hardware acceptance from screenshot smoke. All source changes remain on the PR branch; `gh-pages` and `main` untouched.


### 2026-11-07 — Native preview8: original web workflow + physical USB lifecycle

User feedback: The preview7 native Qt app looked fundamentally unlike the GitHub Pages browser UI and lacked an obvious connect/test/disconnect screen. Requirement: preserve the **web UI's actual receiver/planner/analysis/imagery workflow** while replacing **only WebUSB** with OS-native direct RTL-SDR; do not embed a browser/WebView/Electron or remove features.

**Implemented on this PR branch:**
- **Native web-style seven-section Receiver & planner dashboard:** automatic target, native USB receiver, manual capture (genuine IQ/PCM), station/pass planner, recording calendar, Earth/Sky maps, local RF Signal Intelligence, Satellite Images & Data. Aligns web dark-blue card/button design and clear source metadata; remains Qt Widgets.
- **Hardware / USB:** Linux sysfs USB product/manufacturer/VID:PID inventory distinguishes RTL2832U from Hauppauge DVB television; passive busy-process list; independent `rtl_test` device-open and bounded **1 MiB actual rtl_sdr IQ** test with measured relative digital min/max/RMS. **Connect** requires *both* positive physical tests. **Disconnect** only stops this app's processes, verifies lease exit, persists disabled across restart and pauses pending jobs; never claims electrical power-off or kills readsb.
- **RF output parity:** native full CU8, native FM WAV and CU8+WAV from the same physical recording; ISS auto missions can schedule WAV/CU8/BOTH. Native dual WAV is demodulated **after** IQ capture at 32 kHz, versus the web's live 48 kHz WAV. UI discloses this difference. User-selected 1.024/2.048 MS/s IQ rates have non-silent 2 GB disk caps and truthful estimated space.
- **Genuine native IQ level chart** from an actively growing on-disk CU8 recording (1 Hz read-only sampling, no additional USB ownership).
- **Web-pass tools:** native name/elevation/duration sorting, satellite family/media filtering, local TLE file import, DE/TR offline search, opt-in worldwide city lookup and optional OS-permitted QtPositioning.
- **Satellite Images & Data as its own Qt page:** actual Robot36 and optional SatDump Meteor pipelines; local PNG/WAV/CU8/text previews; online NASA EPIC and historical ISS imagery via bounded official HTTPS requests, source-labeled separately from RF with sidecar metadata. Saved user protocol profiles remain accessible.
- **Build:** independent native Debian package version `0.3.0~preview8`. One-line public GitHub source-based apt installer: `satellite_center/install/install-deb.sh`. Debian offscreen smoke creates **seven** actual Qt screenshots. See `satellite_center/NATIVE_WEB_PARITY.md` for exact semantics/remaining gaps.

**Acceptance boundaries:** Qt/DOM are separate technologies; this is the *same task hierarchy and native UI style*, not a pixel-perfect HTML/CSS clone. Browser-only WebUSB permissions and PWA file pickers should not be mirrored in a native process. Native Windows/macOS packages and physical Pop!_OS COSMIC/Nooelec verification remain outstanding. No fake received images, no automatic RF capture on install. PR **must remain Draft**; `main` and `gh-pages` are deliberately untouched.


### 2026-11-07 — Native preview9: fix full Home pass planner

From user screenshot, **Home → 3 · Satellite pass planner** exposed only Cologne and two buttons, while DE/TR city-region lookup, manual coordinates, worldwide search and meaningful satellite sorting were hidden in a separate view. First-time Calculate passes also did not offer any TLE bootstrap and could leave an unexplained empty list.

**Delivered on PR (native Qt, no WebUSB/WebView):**
- Country Germany / Türkiye, **Bundesland/il** dropdown from actual bundled catalog, local city/town/**known ilçe** lookup with clickable results (8,084 entries; validated NRW→Hürth and İzmir→Karaburun), manually editable lat/lon, 1–72h lookahead and 5–75° minimum elevation **on Home**.
- One-click opt-in worldwide name search via Open-Meteo and optional OS-permitted Qt Positioning; local search uses no network. No claim of exhaustive county/subdistrict registry outside the bundled records.
- **Bidirectional state sharing** between Home and full Passes & Data for coordinates, lookahead and elevation, and exact same Station-derived orbital prediction objects.
- A real Home `QTreeWidget` list with satellite name/NORAD search, family and IMAGE/AUDIO/TEXT/RF filters, 7 sorting modes. Selecting a Home pass selects the **same detailed predicted pass** and opens editable recording/scheduling panel, not a separate fake calendar.
- Calculate now calls `Station.plan_passes`: uses local fresh TLEs where present, otherwise explicitly attempts on-demand real CelesTrak refresh, surfaces empty/no-TLE/network warnings in Home, and does not synthesize RF.
- Same source `sort_filter_passes` logic drives Home and full planner; dedicated offline tests check sort orders, source filtering, caching, country/region names, and Qt GUI smoke asserts Home→plan/schedule routing.
- Debian package bumped to `0.3.0~preview9`; the existing one-line GitHub apt installer automatically reinstalls the updated package. `main` and live `gh-pages` site remain unchanged. Physical Nooelec and COSMIC acceptance not claimed.

**Validation:** follow latest native Debian workflow and unit-test results. Existing Pages/source parity mismatch is a separate unpublished-web-asset gate; do not misrepresent it as native Qt test failure.


### 2026-11-07 — Preview10 exact website UI in installed native receiver

User clarified: The Qt Widgets look/functionality differs significantly from the published website, especially location picker, satellite cards and dropdowns. They want the website's **same exact rendered UI**, while USB capture must be OS-native, never WebUSB; old browser-engine-free requirement clashes with truly identical HTML/CSS. This implementation explicitly supports **both presentation modes**:

- Default `tihulu-satellite-center` (alias `desktop-web`) starts **the SAME bundled `satellite_center/browser/index.html`, CSS, JS modules, maps and UI cards** inside an installed Qt WebEngine window. Uses a custom **secure, path-constrained local scheme** (`tihulu://desktop`), no 127.0.0.1 HTTP server, no external browser window, no WebUSB device access.
- A dedicated **in-process Qt WebChannel** intercepts actual website USB / RF / auto-schedule / pass scheduling controls at capture phase and invokes a strict allowlist of `Station` methods. It uses real installed `rtl_test`, `rtl_sdr`, `rtl_fm` tools via OS. Physical USB verification, actual 1 MiB IQ samples, release/persistence, true disk budgets, TLE validation, local schedule, RF provenance still apply. Native OS confirmation is required for hardware enable, capture and scheduled radio jobs.
- The old **fully browser-engine-free PyQt Widgets** UI is preserved via `tihulu-satellite-center desktop-widgets`. Exact site CSS is otherwise technically impossible without a rendering engine. This difference is disclosed, not hidden.
- The bundled original web page itself is unchanged visually. Hardware wording is replaced only at runtime in the installed native window. Pass cards now add nonvisual NORAD/AOS metadata so native scheduling can validate against a separate Skyfield calculation before acquisition.
- **Sydney typo fix**: both the original website location component and the Qt Widgets fallback resolve `syney` to an actual Open-Meteo **Sydney** query. Coordinates come *only* from real provider results. In the Qt Widgets fallback, user-selecting Worldwide online auto-searches after a debounce, shows suggestions inline and hides empty results/advanced filters by default.
- Debian source installer now builds `0.3.0~preview10`; Qt WebEngine is an explicit Debian dependency; CI tests both Qt Widgets and actual headless bundled-web UI. JavaScript syntax, geocoding and portable runtime checks included.

**Known risks/gates:** actual Qt WebEngine desktop rendering/browser module injection/JS↔Qt transport require successful Debian GUI CI (currently being tested), alongside physical Pop!_OS / Nooelec hardware acceptance. The source-web-vs-gh-pages parity gate is separately pending until reviewed static asset changes are deployed. Keep **PR #18 DRAFT** and `main` untouched. Do not claim pixel-level identical results across differing Chromium versions, fonts, DPI or installed backends, or real ISS/Meteor downlinks from CI.


### 2026-11-07 — Exact shared web UI as native installed Qt desktop

User rejected the replicated Qt Widgets dashboard due to clearly different controls, poor interaction and wrong behavior for **Sydney**. New requirement: reuse the **exact** browser/PWA HTML, CSS and JS visual UI in a locally installed PC app, while ensuring **USB hardware is never controlled by WebUSB**.

- The default installed command `tihulu-satellite-center` now starts `desktop`: Qt WebEngine loads the same local `satellite_center/browser/index.html` and its exact browser assets from the packaged .deb (no remote hosted website, no HTTP listener).
- OS-only physical RTL-SDR operations are behind an allowlisted, **in-process Qt WebChannel** with real user authorization and native `Station` / `rtl_test` / `rtl_sdr` / `rtl_fm`. Capture, scheduled receive, stop, USB test, connect and disconnect buttons are intercepted before the browser's own WebUSB handlers. WebUSB is **not** the SDR transport.
- Website maps, pass planner, local file analysis, image/source panels and styles are shared directly instead of rebuilt with Qt Widgets. An explicit `desktop-widgets` legacy fallback remains for environments where Qt WebEngine is not desired.
- **Native city search fix:** Desktop automatically enables the *existing* opt-out online suggestions toggle, which performs geocoding only when the user types at least three characters with the existing debounce/fair-use safeguards. Shared location script resolves the reported `syney` typo to a **real online Sydney search**; it never guesses/invents lat/lon. The user can uncheck online suggestions for offline-only searches.
- Browser-specific explanatory WebUSB copy is replaced/hidden in the installed desktop, without forking the UI layout. Qt WebEngine is a local rendering engine; this makes exact web CSS/UI possible, although it is inaccurate to describe this frontend as having no embedded browser engine.
- Release package currently `0.3.0~preview10`; Debian CI exercises actual Qt WebEngine startup and produces `08-exact-web.png`. The same one-line installer installs the package.

Safety/acceptance: the shared UI and real native hardware pipeline do **not** establish actual physical Nooelec dongle compatibility or a real satellite decode until user-side test. Pages/source parity is a separate workflow gate; this work does not merge `main` or publish `gh-pages`. PR remains Draft.

pr_records.title: Satellite Center: cross-platform full IQ signal analysis and optional analog audio preview
pr_records.body:
## Existing-project continuation (not a redesign)

Adds the first functional Signal Intelligence slice on top of standalone Satellite Center PR #9, with no changes to main, Flight Radar or Survival Kit.

### Implemented
- Full-file streaming 2048-point CU8 FFT with bounded 256 KiB slices, binned timeline/waterfall, cancellation and clear coverage metrics.
- Explicit unclassified spectral-energy candidate selection; center frequency remains unknown without metadata.
- Experimental local six-second AM/NFM PCM WAV preview at selected baseband offset; this is **not** a satellite decoder or verification of received signal identity.
- Exported user-controlled capture metadata JSON and existing analysis JSON.
- Responsive browser UI, no RF sample uploads, separate quick-sampling mode retained.
- Synthetic tests and Linux ARM / Windows / macOS / Ubuntu CI job expanded to run new Node suite.
- Full cross-platform phases and RF-vs-orbit-vs-Internet source-layer rules in `satellite_center/SIGNAL_INTELLIGENCE.md`.

### Not yet implemented / acceptance required
- End-to-end real SDR and web browser hardware validation.
- Acquisition-time sidecar metadata automation; advanced SigMF import and drift corrections.
- Meteor LRPT/APRS raw-IQ in-browser decoders, interactive spectrum zoom, real RF positioning solutions, live RF source layers.
- Deployment/sync to the separate `gh-pages` publication branch. The public Pages site has **not** been changed.

Keep this PR draft until CI and hardware/browser validation complete. This branch targets the existing Satellite Center feature branch so its changes can flow into PR #9 after review.
